observation: The selected RTL has an 8 KiB global-parameter descriptor SRAM with 64-byte entries, hence 128 entries. A PSS scan DAG with 169 descriptors aliases descriptor indices 128 and above modulo 128 even though payload bytes still fit physical shared SRAM; task 1 block-20 inputs resolve to earlier block descriptors. Repacking the same computation to 85 descriptors eliminates the alias and produces 51/51 exact fresh-RTL returns.

passing.result: prior completing baseline; retained as a bound observation, not an exact capacity proof

failing.result: exact modulo-128 descriptor alias observed in RTL DMA inputs
invalid 0xfb800xxx temporary addresses and no GPIO2

proposed_rule: For RTL commit bf82d804, reject a DAG with more than 128 global-parameter descriptors before Scheduler/RTL handoff; count descriptors, not payload bytes.
When static tables are structurally compatible, pack them into fewer equal-width native vector values without changing fixed-point order or increasing task-local memory traffic.

Before claiming hardware deployability, confirm every temporary AXI write lies inside the backend manifest's physical shared-SRAM aperture and compare every visible return with the qualified Gem5 winner.
Keep 128 backend/RTL-profile scoped; do not apply it to a later RTL generation without checking that generation's descriptor SRAM.
negative_rules: Do not repair invalid packed addresses with an assumed constant pointer offset.
Do not confuse the 128-entry descriptor table with the 512 KiB shared SRAM capacity or the 28-bit source-address field.
Do not promote a candidate merely because all tasks report execute-complete; GPIO completion and returned bytes are required.
Do not replace register-only vector arithmetic with task-local DSPM vstore/vload on this RTL without independent hardware qualification.
review_questions: Should the backend manifest add max_global_parameter_descriptors=128 and the Scheduler adapter reject larger DAGs before firmware build?
Should the toolchain also report descriptor count beside total static payload bytes?
